body: Thanks for the extra context. I can try and reproduce this in the testsuite and seeif we can get a solution, as what you're describing should work.

Thanks for looking into it. i have some variations on my laptop that i tried while we were talking on IRC (none worked at the time), but i'll try them against the current HEAD to see if there's any difference. One variation involved adding `$_accessible['_joinData']` to one of the Entities, but i don't remember which at the moment. It didn't work then, but i'll try again.

-- NOTE --
There's a minor typo in the Table classes code block.  
`class ArticleTable` should read `class ArticlesTable`  
and  
`class ArticleTagsTable` should read `class ArticlesTagsTable`.  
These aren't my actual table names, i was just trying to remain consistent with the documentation example names, but using my own code. The naming is correct in my code or i think i'd see other kinds of errors. :)
I also tried to reproduce this in a test application and wasn't able to make it happen. This [gist](https://gist.github.com/markstory/eb0c170b7852ee20d770) has the code I used.

In the request data, the only difference i can see is my single `tags` sub-array has a numeric "key" corresponding to the array index from the form tying the inputs together, where yours is created raw, so has natural indexes.

Aside from that, there are some small discrepancies between stuff in your gist and my code. For instance i noticed i'm using `'through'` without the other keys, as i assumed convention defaults would handle those. Maybe i'm wrong about that, or mistaken about the convention. i'll specify them to make sure. Your gist's `add` action doesn't save :open_mouth: but otherwise the entity manipulation is exactly the same. Also, if `'_joinData'` is _required_ in the `$_accessible` array for this process, can you make sure it's noted in the Docs at: http://book.cakephp.org/3.0/en/orm/saving-data.html#saving-additional-data-to-the-joint-table

i'll work on it tonight after work & follow up.

@cautionbug The data I have is numerically indexed as well, it just starts at 0. I can try starting at non-zero too.  The controller action intentionally doesn't save as you mentioned the issues was that the hydrated entities were incorrect.

The `_joinData` key _should_ be in _accessible if it is not, however that isn't required as the _joinData is not 'mass assigned'.
Interesting. I will look into why a zero based array is required currently.

Assuming the Table/Entiity classes weren't the cause of the problem, the pivot record wasn't saving at all before PR #6086 when it started partially working, just no `_joinData`. So it _appears_ the index is only problematic there. But i'm obviously no expert.

Thanks for your help with working on this & figuring it out.

issue.body:
When belongsToMany data is sparse the _joinData properties would not be marshalled correctly. By re-indexing the array of data before we marshal it we can ensure the indexes will match up.

Refs #6100
